newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X says has no Indonesia response yet.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X says has no Indonesia response yet.

text.p: Bre-X Minerals Ltd had not yet received an official response from the Indonesian government to Bre-X's joint venture proposal with Barrick Gold Corp, a Bre-X spokesman said on Friday.
"We have not had any official response that I know of from the government," Bre-X spokesman Steve McAnulty said.

Indonesian Mines and Energy Ministry Secretary-General Umar Said told Reuters earlier on Friday that the ministry responded today to the submission from Barrick and Bre-X regarding development of the rich Busang gold discovery.
"We have replied to the letter from Bre-X and Barrick today. The letter says, among other things, that they must settle with their local partners soon," Said said.

He gave no further details, but a ministry source said the government "understood" an agreement between Barrick and Bre-X to divide the richest parts of the Busang gold deposit 67.5 percent for Barrick, 22.5 percent for Bre-X and 10 percent for the Indonesian government.
On Tuesday, as Barrick and Bre-X awaited a government response to their proposal, Canadian miner Placer Dome Inc made a US$5 billion merger offer to Bre-X.
But a source in the ministry told Reuters that the Indonesian government was not likely to accept the involvement of Placer Dome.
On Wednesday, Canadian mining concern Teck Corp threw its hat in the ring and said it hoped to make its own bid for Bre-X and the Busang deposit.
The Busang deposit in Kalimantan on Borneo contains at least 57 million ounces of gold, worth US$21 billion at today's prices.
Many analysts think the property could contain more than 100 million ounces of high-grade, low-cost gold.
But other bidders appeared to be put out of the running for what what was touted as one of the richest gold finds in history last year when Indonesia told Bre-X to forge a deal with Barrick.
